name: The Lost Ingots
summary: The Lost Ingots is an Alliance task in the Wetlands to recover consecrated metal from a shipwreck. After finding only a single bar in a sunken chest, travelers must hunt down the local Bluegill murlocs who looted the remaining shipment.

sections.title: A Plundered Shipwreck
sections.body: Off the misty shores of the Wetlands lies the shattered wreckage of the Flying Osprey. Sent to retrieve precious Lightforge iron for the dwarven priest Glorin Steelbrow, seekers discovered that the cargo hold's waterlogged chest was nearly empty. The ravenous local Bluegill murlocs had already scavenged the rest of the vessel, taking the gleaming ingots for themselves.

sections.title: Reclaiming the Sacred Metal
sections.body: Lightforge iron is no ordinary ore; it is rare, specialized metal attuned to work sacred smithing craft. Allowing it to rot in murloc encampments is unthinkable for a dwarf of the Light. By hunting down the Bluegill raiders swarming the shallows near the broken hull, adventurers prise back the scattered bars so Glorin Steelbrow can see the iron hammered into a weapon.

faq.q: What ship carried the Lightforge iron?
faq.answer: The cargo arrived aboard the Flying Osprey, an unfortunate vessel that met its demise off the coast of the Wetlands. Its broken timbers now lie partially submerged in the shallows.

faq.q: Why were the ingots not in the chest?
faq.answer: Only a single ingot remained locked within the waterlogged chest. The coastal Bluegill murlocs had already pried into the sunken wreckage and scavenged the rest of the shipment to scatter among their coastal raiders.

Glorin Steelbrow is a dwarven priest of the Church of the Holy Light, found in the Deepwater Tavern in Menethil Harbor. A colleague of Bishop Farthing, he seeks Lightforge iron so a weapon can be forged against the necromancer Morbent Fel.

faq.q: What is special about Lightforge iron?
faq.answer: Lightforge iron is a rare, sanctified metal uniquely receptive to holy enchantments and smithing. It is prized by artisans crafting armaments aligned with the Holy Light.
The Bluegill tribe, specifically the murloc raiders that prowl the shallows and beaches around the wreckage of the Flying Osprey, seized the missing bars.

faq.q: What comes next after returning the ingots?
faq.answer: Once Glorin Steelbrow receives the full set of ingots, he packs the sanctified metal into a crate and sends you to the weaponsmith Grimand Elmore in Stormwind to have it forged, continuing in Blessed Arm.

angles.text: Recovering lost masterwork ore and putting it into the hands of a dwarven priest like Glorin Steelbrow honors the long tradition of dwarven craftsmanship and reclaimers.
Reclaiming Lightforge iron from primitive murlocs ensures holy materials are preserved to fashion consecrated weaponry fit to champion the Light.
Every metalworker knows the tragedy of seeing superior stock like Lightforge iron end up as curios in a coastal murloc nest instead of an anvil.
